opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st October 2026 (bi-monthly: 1st of February, April, June, August, October and December)

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored up to £750); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members: Scheme A open to undergraduate, Master's and PhD students and postdocs within 6 years of PhD viva; Schemes B & C open to PhD students and postdocs within 6 years of PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or talk at the conference. UK base required for non-UK conferences (and vice versa).
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of junior scientist members at genetics research conferences. Three streams: (A) GS/SIG meetings travel & accommodation up to £200; (B) non-GS meetings travel, accommodation & registration up to £500 (Adelphi co-sponsored up to £750); (C) virtual conference registration up to £300.

opportunities.title: Training Grant

deadlines.raw: 15th November 2026 (quarterly: 15th February, May, August and November)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or where the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable members to attend formal short training courses or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Covers travel and accommodation costs associated with a field-based genetic research project, funded by income from the Society's journal Heredity. Research should produce results suitable for publication in Heredity.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member can apply, regardless of age of the person they care for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need. Awards must be applied for prior to the meeting/event and are competitive.
opportunities.summary: Provides an award of up to £60/day to support members with caring responsibilities to attend Society meetings and events, to be used as the awardee thinks best supports their attendance.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Grant

amount.raw: Several levels of sponsorship; a GS lecture for a few hundred pounds, a GS session up to ~£1,000, major sponsorship of an entire meeting potentially several thousand pounds (major sponsorship last 12 months between £1,000 and £2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Members may apply at any time of the year, ideally at least three months before the event.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of one-off genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society, used towards organisation of a meeting (not attendance).

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st October 2026 (two deadlines per year: 1st March and 1st October)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to members of the Genetics Society. Funding may cover eligible travel (budget/economy class, UK-based only) and materials costs.
opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Cannot be used for salaries, institutional overheads, room hire in academic institutions, for-profit media, or research data collection.

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Applications to become a new SIG should be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes, for genetics research communities wishing to run regular series of meetings (e.g. Seed Plant, e-ACGT, C. elegans Group, London Genetics Network).
